identity.title: Retrieval-Augmented Perception: High-resolution Image Perception Meets Visual RAG

problem.claim: Improve high-resolution image perception in multimodal large language models.

gap.claim: The paper identifies limits in heuristic methods and explores whether long-context retrieval-augmented generation can address them.

contributions.claim: Retrieval-Augmented Perception (RAP), a training-free framework that retrieves and fuses relevant image crops while preserving spatial context through a Spatial-Awareness Layout.
Retrieved-Exploration Search (RE-Search), which dynamically selects the number of crops using model confidence and retrieval scores for different tasks.
A first study of using retrieval-augmented generation for high-resolution perception challenges.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that this is the first study exploring RAG for high-resolution perception challenges.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that RAP improved LLaVA-v1.5-13B performance by 43% on V* Bench and 19% on HR-Bench.

narrative_sequence.summary: High-resolution image perception is presented as a key challenge for multimodal large language models.
The paper seeks to move beyond heuristic methods by applying long-context techniques such as retrieval-augmented generation.
RAP retrieves and fuses image crops while retaining spatial context through a Spatial-Awareness Layout.
RE-Search chooses the crop count dynamically from model confidence and retrieval scores.
On high-resolution benchmarks, the authors report substantial gains for LLaVA-v1.5-13B.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns each proposed component with a concrete operational challenge: spatial context is handled by the layout, while task variation is handled by dynamic crop selection.

lessons.interpretation: This makes the method narrative explanatory rather than presenting a collection of unrelated mechanisms.
lessons.application: When introducing a multi-part method, map each component explicitly to the failure mode or requirement it addresses.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when component roles cannot be distinguished or supported independently.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the baselines, evaluation protocols, statistical uncertainty, or whether the reported percentage improvements are relative or absolute.
The abstract does not provide details about the HR benchmarks, tasks, or computational cost of retrieval and crop fusion.
